thread:
ana: Alert - committed capacity near saturation in ap-south-1. seeing large queue growth and admission control kicking. :rotating_light:
infra-bot: [ALERT] committed-pool-low-capacity ap-south-1 (severity: high) — 95% queue length, 8m sustained. link: https://internal.metrics/pools/ap-south-1
mike_oncall: I'm on it, pulling recent allocator logs and queue histograms. can someone confirm a customer spike?
kevin: PulseAI has a batch job started ~06:10 UTC hitting our dedicated commit for ap-south-1, looks like a misconfigured job fanout across pinned region.
sre_tess: queue growth graph: ```queue_length: 3400 -> 9800 (6m), admission_rate down 60% -> 20%``` backlog is mostly requests waiting >3s for admit.
ops_lee: fallback routing to hosted triggered automatically for some routes. that means extra ingress to hosted API and a cost spike in the last 10m. need to avoid cascading.
nana: (typo) sorry, ana again — turning off fallback would cause user-facing errors, we should throttle low-priority tenants first.
kevin: I think the autoscaler policy for this committed pool is using `cpu_util` instead of `queue_depth` metric due to a recent policy rename. it never ramped to handle the surge.
mike_oncall: confirmed. logs show scale decision skipped: `scale_decision: metric_missing(queue_depth)`. rolling a hotfix to include queue_depth in policy now.
kevin: immediate mitigations: 1) tighten admission control for non-enterprise tenants 2) lower per-request concurrency to release GPUs 3) temporarily increase fair-share weight for enterprise commits
mike_oncall: running: ```curl -XPOST https://controlplane/api/pools/ap-south-1/actions -d '{"set_admission_limit": 350, "priority_cutoff": "tier:enterprise"}'```
infra-bot: action completed: set_admission_limit=350, priority_cutoff=tier:enterprise (by mike_oncall). new admission policy will be active in ~30s.
sre_tess: admission rates improving, queue length dropping from 9800 -> 4200 in 2m. hosted fallback traffic decreasing but still elevated.
ops_lee: billing watch: hosted egress token cost estimated +18% last 15m because of fallback. opened JIRA INC-3498 to track cost remediation.
prod-alex: impact to SLOs? any customers exposed?
mike_oncall: enterprise customers should be fine due to priority cutoff. some low-tier customers saw increased latency or errors earlier; we throttled them to preserve capacity. preparing an incident notice.
sre_tess: long term follow-ups: 1) fix autoscaler metric config rollback 2) add preflight checks on policy renames 3) emergency throttle runbook update to include cost-control step 4) migrate PulseAI batch jobs to shared-burst pool for large spikes
kevin: agreed. also adding a stat to the dashboard: `committed_pool_queue_depth_per_tenant` so we can auto-detect noisy tenants earlier.
nana: (again typo) thanks everyone. will draft postmortem and severity timeline. next steps: postmortem + customer communications + quota adjustments.
prod-alex: noted, please tag me on the postmortem.
mike_oncall: closing actions for now — pools stabilizing, autoscaler hotfix queued for deploy. will report back when hotfix is live. :white_check_mark:
